assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational body of political-economy research connecting political institutions, state capacity, fiscal policy, and development outcomes.
assessment.attribution: These three scholars are central, complementary contributors to the theoretical and empirical political-economy agenda described.
assessment.maturity: The work has shaped research and policy analysis over several decades and has a broad, durable empirical and conceptual legacy.
uncertainties: The contribution spans several connected literatures, making a sharply bounded single discovery harder to state.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence methods made discrimination measurable in consequential real-world settings and transformed empirical labour economics.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan's field-experimental contribution is especially identifiable within the stated discovery.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been extensively replicated, extended, and incorporated into public and scholarly debate.
uncertainties: Audit-study estimates identify important mechanisms but their interpretation can remain context-dependent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This research substantially changed understanding of how trade and technology reshape local labour markets, occupations, and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson form a coherent core for the trade-shock and task-based empirical programme.
assessment.maturity: Its findings stimulated a large subsequent literature and remain central to analysis of distributional consequences of globalization.
uncertainties: Separating trade effects from technology and other local adjustments remains empirically demanding.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data have yielded an influential and concrete account of intergenerational mobility and geographic inequality of opportunity.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are the most clearly identifiable central contributors to the stated mobility research programme.
assessment.maturity: The evidence base is extensive and the work has strongly redirected research and public discussion of opportunity.
uncertainties: Measures of mobility do not by themselves establish which policies will causally improve opportunity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Law-and-finance research created a highly influential framework for studying how legal institutions affect investor protection and financial development.
assessment.attribution: La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, and Shleifer are central authors of the core legal-origins research.
assessment.maturity: The agenda has had long-lasting influence across finance, development, and institutional political economy.
uncertainties: The causal interpretation and universality of legal-origin claims have been substantially debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The creation and analysis of long-run income, wealth, and offshore-wealth data have fundamentally enlarged empirical knowledge of inequality.
assessment.attribution: Piketty, Saez, and Zucman are prominent and closely associated contributors to the listed measurement and analysis programme.
assessment.maturity: The work has generated major scholarly influence, new data infrastructure, and sustained international research.
uncertainties: Historical and cross-border wealth measurement necessarily depends on incomplete records and modeling choices.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work brought exhaustible resources, biodiversity, and natural capital into rigorous long-run economic accounting and welfare analysis.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal are both foundational contributors to the stated environmental-economics contribution.
assessment.maturity: The framework is mature and increasingly important for policy, although biodiversity accounting remains an evolving application.
uncertainties: Valuing ecological systems and translating inclusive-wealth measures into policy involve substantial conceptual and empirical uncertainty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification supplied a disciplined alternative to unwarranted point identification and improved the credibility of empirical conclusions under weak assumptions.
assessment.attribution: Manski established the core programme, with Tamer and Molinari making major contributions to moment inequalities and implementation.
assessment.maturity: The methods are well developed and influential across econometrics and applied work.
uncertainties: Its impact is methodological and may be less publicly legible than discoveries with a more direct substantive application.
